standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverse
standard_prerequisites.statement: qinv(f) is the type of pairs (g, g o f ~ id) x (f o g ~ id).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose equivalence with the self-homotopies of the identity is asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence and idtoeqv
standard_prerequisites.statement: idtoeqv : (A = B) -> (A ~ B) is an equivalence, so by univalence any equivalence may be assumed to be of the form idtoeqv(p).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction performed at source line 48.

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality
standard_prerequisites.statement: Homotopies may be replaced by equalities of functions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used twice, at source lines 55-56 and at line 62.

core_obligations: Use the hypothesis that qinv f is inhabited to get an equivalence (f,e) : A ~ B (source line 47).
By univalence assume that this equivalence is idtoeqv(p) for some p : A = B, and then by path induction assume p is reflexivity, so that f is the identity (source lines 48-49).
Reduce to the case f = id, where qinv(id) unfolds to Sigma g, (g ~ id) x (g ~ id) (source lines 50-54).
Apply function extensionality to turn the two homotopies into equalities and reassociate the sigma type (source lines 55-60).

Use that Sigma g, (g = id) is contractible with centre (id, refl), apply the omission-of-contractible-components result to reduce to id = id, and apply function extensionality once more to reach prd x:A (x = x) (source lines 61-62).

proof_roadmap.step: Univalence and path induction reduce to the identity function.
Unfold qinv of the identity, apply extensionality and reassociate.
Contract the sigma type, omit the contractible component and apply extensionality.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:qinv-autohtpy` at source lines 42-45: if qinv f is inhabited then qinv(f) is equivalent to prd x:A (x = x). The author's proof (source lines 46-63) is a chain of reductions rather than a direct construction: univalence turns the assumed quasi-inverse into an equivalence which may be assumed to be idtoeqv of a path (lines 47-48), path induction then reduces f to the identity function (line 49), and only then does the computation start, unfolding qinv of the identity into a sigma type of homotopies (lines 51-54), applying function extensionality to replace homotopies by equalities (lines 55-56), reassociating (lines 57-60), contracting the sigma type of g together with g = id and omitting that contractible component (line 61), and finally applying extensionality again to obtain the type of self-homotopies of the identity (line 62). Three separate standard results are consumed in a fixed order, and the statement shows none of them.
